operations.reason: Specify each user-facing path contract, resolution root, existence rule, and existing owner while preserving both agent-work-dir syntaxes, precedence, log fallback, and durable cleanup behavior.

edits.replacement: Preserve --agent-work-dir <path> and --agent-work-dir=<path>. The pre-init scan must normalize both forms to one non-empty, NUL-free path value before initContainer(), then pass that value through the existing resolver. The inventory records this as a required value option accepting absolute or repository-root-relative paths, naming a directory, with no pre-existence requirement and no new size bound; src/sennel.js, resolveWorkDir, and container initialization own parsing, resolution, creation/use, and errors. Preserve precedence invocation override > config.agent.workDir > .tmp, explicit config.logs.dir resolved against the repository root (or the durable root for finalize-cleanup) > agentWorkDir/logs fallback, and the durable main-repository root used by finalize-cleanup. The per-leaf path inventory is concrete: run gate --spec accepts the existing canonical Spec directory or its spec.json path, absolute or execution-root-relative, and requires the existing target resolved by the gate owner; set review-evidence --file accepts an existing non-symlink regular JSON file, bounded by the existing review-evidence limit, inside the active spec directory resolved from the execution root; get context path is an optional project-root-relative file path whose existing file is read in file mode, while omission selects list mode and --search is a query value; set files reqId paths requires at least one non-empty rest path and delegates path mapping, count, and aggregate-size rules to FlowManager.updateFileMap without inventing existence checks; and set issue-log --repair-ref-file is a non-empty path string whose commit/file reference validation remains with the issue-log owner. For every path row, record file versus directory, existence, absolute/relative support, resolution root, and the existing size or no-bound owner. Output directories need not pre-exist. Runtime initialization, log writing, cleanup, and all command-specific path/domain validation remain owned by their existing modules; this requirement adds no blanket path validator or unrelated restriction.

operations.reason: Replace grouped owner references with a per-leaf validation inventory, explicit positional/type/path distinctions, and named existing size and validator owners without creating a parallel validator.

edits.replacement: The shared option authority is projected into the existing parser and help for every shared routed leaf, while flow query remains an independent custom-parser exception. The Spec inventory is a concrete table with one row for every registry leaf and columns for exact positionals, rest values, flags, required-value options, optional-value options, implicit help, arity, required/optional cardinality, type, format, domain/range, empty behavior, existing size bound or explicit absence with owner, conditional combinations, path kind, existence, absolute/relative support, resolution root, applicable target guards, parser owner, semantic validator owner, and test owner. The shared model owns only syntax/help projection and the delegation boundary; parseEntryInput owns argv syntax, FlowTargetExpectation and buildFlowCommandHookContext own the five target guards, and each existing command/registry validator owns semantic values and state-dependent combinations. Record these concrete distinctions: set step status, set auto value, and set broad action are positional values; get status runId is optional; set files requires at least one rest path; resume --spec is a FlowSpecId; run gate --spec is a filesystem Spec directory or spec.json path; prepare --base and run lint --base are Git branch names; prepare --run-id is a PreparingFlowId with its existing 200-character/no-colon owner; runtime-log --run-id is its runId plus optional sequence form; and target guard tokens use FlowTargetExpectation and its existing 300-character rule, not a generic ID rule. The table must name the existing owner for get check target, get prompt kind, artifact logicalKey, step id/status, note text, draft questionId, requirement reqId, --format, --mode, --phase, --sequence, --category, --record-category, --step, --task-id, --normalized-finding-id, --repair-ref-commit, --repair-ref-file, --expect-attempt-id, --approve, and --choice, including each value's applicable combinations. It must also record existing text/JSON/path sizes, set-files count and aggregate limits, exclusions serialized size, retry/attempt limits, query request-file limits, context traversal/read limits, and review-evidence limits, or state that no explicit bound exists and identify the owner. No shared validator, copied command decision, arbitrary tighter limit, or query admission rule is introduced.

edits.replacement: For every applicable shared routed leaf, existing parser failures, unknown or missing selectors, missing values, extra positionals, option-domain failures, the --expect-issue/--expect-no-issue mutual exclusion, and the five target mismatches stop before command-owned mutation with the existing diagnostic, exit code 1, and rejection order. The input inventory records --expect-binding <token> as a non-empty base64url JSON FlowTargetBinding decoded by FlowTargetBinding.deserialize, with the existing 32 KiB byte limit and structural/authority validation; --expect-issue <number> as a positive safe integer; --expect-no-issue as a valueless flag; --expect-spec <spec> as a FlowSpecId; and --expect-run-id <runId> as the existing non-empty FlowTargetExpectation token up to 300 characters. Binding runId, issue, spec, and authority identity must match through the existing FlowTargetBinding/FlowTargetExpectation owner, and the applicable leaf set is derived from the registry. Test a valid match, a mismatch for each guard, invalid syntax/value, and the issue/no-issue conflict through FlowTargetExpectation and buildFlowCommandHookContext before handler mutation. Omission of all guards is the defined retained unguarded behavior: the command follows its existing leaf validation and lifecycle, and the Spec test records that case separately. No blanket validator, new ID limit, or new target decision is introduced.

**Target:** Acceptance Criteria; R1/R2; T-9
**Issue:** FLOW_COMMANDS currently contains 35 run leaves, including flow run report, plus report show. The non-query routed set is therefore 66 leaves, not the specified 65.

**Why blocking:** The required registry and behavior matrices can omit flow run report, whose registry entry has pre/post/onError hooks, leaving existing behavior untested and the implementation target undefined.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec's acceptance criteria still describe a 65-leaf shared set while the review identifies flow run report as an additional non-query leaf. R1/R2 and T-9 need the count and deterministic matrix ownership reconciled together.

finding.body:
**Target:** R4/R8; src/sennel.js
**Issue:** The dispatcher accepts --agent-work-dir=<path>, but src/sennel.js pre-scans only the separate-token form before initContainer(). Consequently, equals-form invocations currently use config/default paths while separate-form invocations use the invocation override.
**Required change:** State explicitly that equals-form pre-init parity is the intended compatibility correction, and change the R4 wording that currently claims both existing forms already preserve the same resolver behavior.
**Why blocking:** Without resolving this contradiction, runtime and log tests cannot determine whether to preserve the current divergent paths or normalize both forms; the wrong choice can send agent files and logs to a different work directory.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec's R4 wording says both agent-work-dir forms preserve existing resolver behavior, while R8 requires pre-init normalization. The review's source observation identifies the equals-form pre-scan gap, so the compatibility correction must be stated explicitly in the Spec wording.

finding.body:
**Target:** R1/R2; T-1/T-2; Acceptance Criteria
**Issue:** The current registry args contain mostly positional/flag/option name arrays, while semantic validation is distributed across command modules, FlowTargetExpectation, and path/Git helpers. The spec requires an individual inventory but does not provide one or map every leaf input to its existing owner. This matters for same-named inputs with different contracts, such as --spec on resume versus run gate, --run-id on preparing-flow commands versus runtime-log, and --base on prepare versus lint.
**Required change:** Add a concrete inventory for every current routed leaf that maps each input to its kind, value/domain/path contract, conditional combination, existing validator owner, and test owner, including distinctions for same-named inputs.
**Why blocking:** An implementer can otherwise centralize or tighten a command-owned rule accidentally, and tests cannot derive the expected valid/invalid argv, diagnostic owner, or rejection order.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec requires per-leaf inventory and validator ownership in R1/R2, but its requirements, tasks, and acceptance criteria provide only aggregate examples and no concrete inventory for every routed leaf. The missing detail spans the two requirement descriptions, T-1/T-2 implementation notes, and their acceptance evidence.

finding.body:
**Target:** Acceptance Criteria (65-leaf success matrix); T-9
**Issue:** The acceptance criteria require a valid normal-success invocation for every leaf, but the registry includes AI-driven, finalization, recovery, and state-transition commands with incompatible prerequisites. The tasks only name representative suites and provide no per-leaf production fixture, state setup, agent boundary, or mutation assertion.
**Required change:** Add a deterministic legal success fixture and owning test boundary for each registry leaf, including its required Flow state and external-agent handling, and reconcile T-9's representative-only wording with that universal criterion.
**Why blocking:** Tests would either invoke unsafe state mutations/agent execution ad hoc or omit leaves while still appearing representative, so the required all-leaf behavior cannot be implemented and verified deterministically.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec has a universal per-leaf success criterion for 65 leaves but T-9 still assigns only representative suites and does not provide deterministic legal fixtures, state setup, or agent-boundary ownership for every leaf. The acceptance matrix and T-9 implementation notes must be reconciled.
